description: Feasibility probe, run after calibration and before the unattended campaign. Calibration measured the publisher's ceiling only at 16 clients, so it cannot say what one client or sixty-four can deliver, and it never tested a 100-byte row or a 1000-row commit. Families B, C and D need those numbers to choose a fixed byte rate that every level in the family can actually hold. Every level here is unthrottled: the number that matters is measured_wal_mb_per_sec, which IS the ceiling for that combination.

levels.label: 1 client, 10 rows/commit - the binding constraint for family B
100-byte rows, 1 row/commit - the binding constraint for family D
100-byte rows at 64 clients - can more clients lift family D?
1000 rows/commit - the far end of family C
